lesson.menu_desc: Halfway through the program: review the tenses of Lessons 11-20 on one time map (past simple, present perfect, been + -ing, used to, will / going to, if), learn the words of fluency — hesitate, filler, rephrase, setback — and measure your speaking in three timed tasks, then set goals for Lessons 22-43.
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 21 — Mid-Program Review: Speaking Fluency Check
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Daniela Feitoza | Lesson 21 -- Mid-Program Review: Speaking Fluency Check

listenings.text: Hi Daniela, it is Sarah, your English coach. You are halfway through the program, so today let us talk about fluency. Fluency is not perfect English. Fluency means you keep going. Everybody hesitates, even native speakers. The problem is not the pause. The problem is silence that goes on and on. So, three tips. First, use smart fillers. Instead of a long silence, or umm, umm, umm, say: let me think, or that is a good question. A filler gives you two seconds, and you still sound in control. Second, if you forget a word, do not stop. Rephrase. Say it another way. If you forget the word deadline, say: the date when the project has to be ready. People will understand you. Third, after a setback, keep talking. A setback is a small problem, not the end. If you make a mistake, correct it quickly and continue. And one last thing. Leave your comfort zone a little every week. Speak in the meeting, ask the question, tell the story. That is how real progress happens. You have already made a lot of progress, Daniela. Now set one goal for the next month, and keep going. Talk soon.

Hi Daniela, it is Greg. I am calling with some quick feedback after our mid-year check-in. First, congratulations. Six months ago, you used to plan every sentence before a meeting. Now you speak much more freely. Last month you gave the SAP talk at the conference, and the team loved it. You have also run three project calls in English since July, and that is real progress. Of course, there was one setback. On the call with the London team, you hesitated a lot when they asked about the budget. That is normal. Next time, use a filler, take two seconds, and answer. My suggestion for the next quarter is simple. You are going to lead the weekly status call with the US team, starting in November. If you prepare three key points before each call, you will feel much more confident. Let us review your goals again in December. Great work, Daniela. Talk soon.

extra_audio.text: First, Daniela looked back at where she started: she used to plan every sentence in Portuguese. Then she listed what she has done since then: she has given a talk and run three calls in English. After that, she named one setback: she hesitated on the budget question. Next, she explained what she has been doing to improve: she has been using smart fillers. Finally, she set a goal: she is going to lead the weekly status call in November.
